description.text:
The first expansion pack of the Pokémon Card Game, then called the Pocket Monsters Card Game, released in Japan on 20 October 1996 alongside the first Starter Pack. Creatures developed the game and Media Factory published it. Its Pokémon include Venusaur, Charizard and Blastoise, and its Trainers the basics the game long relied on: Professor Oak and Bill to draw cards, Pokémon Center and Potion to heal, Gust of Wind and Energy Removal to hold the opponent back. Sales were slow at first, but by the end of the year the cards were the ninth best-selling item across Ito-Yokado's stores. In the United States the same cards came out as Base Set on 9 January 1999.

The set's first print carries no 1st Edition stamp. Instead it has no rarity mark in the bottom right corner, where later prints show a circle, diamond or star, and collectors call it "No Rarity". Only the earliest booster packs and starter decks hold them, from a short first print run, and a few of them, among them Venusaur, Charizard, Raichu and Gastly, carry errors that the later print corrected.

description.text: Machamp was a holo rare of Japan's first expansion, sold in Expansion Pack boosters from October 20, 1996, more than two years before the English card. The Japanese cards carry no set number; No. 068 is Machamp's Pokédex number. Unlike the English Machamp, it came in booster packs. Its Pokédex entry comes from Pokémon Red and Green, where the English card's comes from Red and Blue.

description.text: The first Japanese print, with no rarity symbol beside the number at the bottom right; later prints added a star. Collectors call this run No Rarity Base Set and take it for the earliest, since it has errors that were fixed later, such as Venusaur numbered 068, Machamp's number, instead of 003.
